name: isRestricted.smul'
statement:
lemma isRestricted.smul' {K : Type*} [Semiring K] [Module K R] [IsScalarTower K R R] (c : σ → ℝ)
    (k : K) {f : MvPowerSeries σ R} (hf : IsRestricted c f) : IsRestricted c (k • f)
doc: /-- Scalars acting on the coefficients through the ring `R` preserve restrictedness. -/

name: algebraMap_eq_C_comp
statement:
lemma algebraMap_eq_C_comp {S K : Type*} [NormedCommRing S] [IsUltrametricDist S] [CommSemiring K]
    [Algebra K S] : algebraMap K (Restricted S c) = (C c).comp (algebraMap K S)

name: norm_prod_pow_le_of_norm_le
statement:
theorem norm_prod_pow_le_of_norm_le [NormOneClass B] (hx : ∀ i, ‖x i‖ ≤ c i) (t : σ →₀ ℕ) :
    ‖t.prod fun i k ↦ x i ^ k‖ ≤ 1 * t.prod (c · ^ ·)
doc:
/-- The monomials of a tuple with `‖x i‖ ≤ c i` are bounded by the monomials of the polyradius,
when `‖1‖ ≤ 1`. -/

name: exists_forall_norm_prod_pow_le
statement:
theorem exists_forall_norm_prod_pow_le [Finite σ] (hx : ∀ i, ∃ Cx, ∀ k, ‖x i ^ k‖ ≤ Cx) :
    ∃ Cx, ∀ t : σ →₀ ℕ, ‖t.prod fun i k ↦ x i ^ k‖ ≤ Cx * t.prod ((1 : σ → ℝ) · ^ ·)
doc:
/-- The monomials of finitely many power-bounded elements are bounded: `‖x^ν‖ ≤ M` for all `ν`.
Source: BGR 1.2.5/2 (power-bounded elements form a ring), 6.1.1/4 (the series `Σ φ(a_ν) f^ν`
converges because the `fᵢ` are power-bounded). -/

name: norm_map_mul_prod_pow_le
statement:
theorem norm_map_mul_prod_pow_le (hφ : ∀ r, ‖φ r‖ ≤ Cφ * ‖r‖)
    (hx : ∀ t : σ →₀ ℕ, ‖t.prod fun i k ↦ x i ^ k‖ ≤ Cx * t.prod (c · ^ ·)) (a : R)
    (t : σ →₀ ℕ) : ‖φ a * t.prod fun i k ↦ x i ^ k‖ ≤ Cφ * Cx * (‖a‖ * t.prod (c · ^ ·))
doc: /-- Each term of the evaluated series is bounded by the corresponding Gauss term. -/

name: tendsto_map_coeff_mul_prod_pow
statement:
theorem tendsto_map_coeff_mul_prod_pow (hφ : ∀ r, ‖φ r‖ ≤ Cφ * ‖r‖)
    (hx : ∀ t : σ →₀ ℕ, ‖t.prod fun i k ↦ x i ^ k‖ ≤ Cx * t.prod (c · ^ ·)) (f : Restricted R c) :
    Tendsto (fun t : σ →₀ ℕ ↦ φ (coeff t f.1) * t.prod fun i k ↦ x i ^ k) cofinite (𝓝 0)
doc: /-- The terms of the evaluated series tend to zero. -/

name: norm_eval₂_le_mul
statement:
theorem norm_eval₂_le_mul [Fact (∀ i, 0 < c i)] (f : Restricted R c) :
    ‖eval₂ c φ x hφ hx f‖ ≤ Cφ * Cx * ‖f‖
doc: /-- Evaluation is bounded by the product of the bounds. Source: BGR 5.1.4/2, 6.1.1/4. -/

name: _root_.TopologicalRing.IsBounded.exists_norm_le_of_normedAlgebra
statement:
theorem _root_.TopologicalRing.IsBounded.exists_norm_le_of_normedAlgebra {S : Set R}
    (hS : TopologicalRing.IsBounded S) : ∃ C, ∀ s ∈ S, ‖s‖ ≤ C
doc:
/-- In a normed algebra over a nontrivially normed field, a bounded set is bounded in norm: a
scalar of small norm multiplies it into the unit ball. Source: BGR 1.2.5/1 (power-boundedness as
boundedness of `{|aⁿ|}`), Wedhorn, Example 5.29(2). -/

name: IsPowerBounded.exists_norm_pow_le
statement:
theorem IsPowerBounded.exists_norm_pow_le {a : R} (ha : IsPowerBounded a) :
    ∃ C, ∀ n : ℕ, ‖a ^ n‖ ≤ C
doc:
/-- A power-bounded element of a normed algebra over a nontrivially normed field has bounded
powers in norm. Source: BGR 1.2.5/1. -/

name: IsPowerBounded.map
doc:
/-- A bounded ring homomorphism maps power-bounded elements to power-bounded elements.
Source: BGR 6.1.1 ("Morphisms of `𝔄` map power-bounded elements into power-bounded elements"). -/

name: isUltrametricDist
statement: instance isUltrametricDist : IsUltrametricDist (M ⧸ S)
doc:
/-- The quotient seminorm of an ultrametric seminormed group is ultrametric: the infimum over
cosets of an ultrametric norm. Source: BGR 1.1.6 (the residue norm of a quotient group). -/

name: norm_mk_eq_norm_of_forall_le
statement:
theorem norm_mk_eq_norm_of_forall_le {f : R} (h : ∀ a ∈ I, ‖f‖ ≤ ‖f - a‖) :
    ‖Ideal.Quotient.mk I f‖ = ‖f‖
doc:
/-- The quotient norm of a residue class is attained by a representative whenever some
representative has the smallest norm in its coset. -/

name: normOneClass_of_ne_top
statement:
theorem normOneClass_of_ne_top (I : Ideal R) [IsClosed (I : Set R)] (hI : I ≠ ⊤) :
    NormOneClass (R ⧸ I)
doc:
/-- In a complete nonarchimedean normed ring with `‖1‖ = 1`, every element at distance less than
one from `1` is a unit, so the residue class of `1` modulo a proper closed ideal has norm one.
Source: BGR 1.2.4/4 and 6.1.1 (the residue norm). -/

name: norm_sumTuple_le
statement: theorem norm_sumTuple_le (i : σ ⊕ τ) : ‖sumTuple R c i‖ ≤ c i

name: iterToSum_comp_sumToIter
statement:
theorem iterToSum_comp_sumToIter :
    (iterToSum (R := R) c).comp (sumToIter c) = RingHom.id (Restricted R c)

name: sumToIter_comp_iterToSum
statement:
theorem sumToIter_comp_iterToSum :
    (sumToIter (R := R) c).comp (iterToSum c) =
      RingHom.id (Restricted (Restricted R (c ∘ Sum.inr)) (c ∘ Sum.inl))

name: sumEquiv_C
statement: theorem sumEquiv_C (r : R) : sumEquiv c (C c r) = C (c ∘ Sum.inl) (C (c ∘ Sum.inr) r)

name: sumEquiv_X_inl
statement:
theorem sumEquiv_X_inl (i : σ) :
    sumEquiv c (X R c (Sum.inl i)) = X (Restricted R (c ∘ Sum.inr)) (c ∘ Sum.inl) i

name: sumEquiv_X_inr
statement:
theorem sumEquiv_X_inr (j : τ) :
    sumEquiv c (X R c (Sum.inr j)) = C (c ∘ Sum.inl) (X R (c ∘ Sum.inr) j)

name: norm_sumEquiv
statement: theorem norm_sumEquiv (f : Restricted R c) : ‖sumEquiv (R := R) c f‖ = ‖f‖
doc: /-- The isomorphism `R⟨X ⊕ Y⟩ ≅ R⟨Y⟩⟨X⟩` is isometric for the Gauss norms. -/

name: continuous_sumEquiv
statement: theorem continuous_sumEquiv : Continuous (sumEquiv (R := R) c)

name: continuous_sumEquiv_symm
statement: theorem continuous_sumEquiv_symm : Continuous (sumEquiv (R := R) c).symm

name: renameEquiv
statement:
noncomputable def renameEquiv (e : σ ≃ τ) :
    Restricted R (1 : σ → ℝ) ≃+* Restricted R (1 : τ → ℝ)
doc:
/-- Renaming the variables of a strictly convergent power series along a bijection `e : σ ≃ τ`,
at the unit polyradius. Source: BGR 5.1.3 (a chart is a renaming of the variables). -/

name: renameEquiv_C
statement: theorem renameEquiv_C (r : R) : renameEquiv R e (C (1 : σ → ℝ) r) = C (1 : τ → ℝ) r

name: renameEquiv_X
statement: theorem renameEquiv_X (i : σ) : renameEquiv R e (X R (1 : σ → ℝ) i) = X R (1 : τ → ℝ) (e i)

name: norm_renameEquiv
statement: theorem norm_renameEquiv (f : Restricted R (1 : σ → ℝ)) : ‖renameEquiv R e f‖ = ‖f‖
doc: /-- Renaming the variables is an isometry for the Gauss norms. -/

name: sumEquiv
statement:
noncomputable def sumEquiv :
    Restricted (TateAlgebra K n) (1 : Fin m → ℝ) ≃ₐ[K] TateAlgebra K (m + n)
doc:
/-- `Tₙ⟨Y₁, …, Y_m⟩ ≅ T_{m+n}` as `K`-algebras, isometrically: the sum isomorphism followed by the
renaming `Fin m ⊕ Fin n ≃ Fin (m + n)`. Source: BGR 6.1.1/8 (`T_m ⊗̂_k Tₙ ≅ T_{m+n}`). -/

name: norm_sumEquiv
statement:
theorem norm_sumEquiv (f : Restricted (TateAlgebra K n) (1 : Fin m → ℝ)) :
    ‖sumEquiv K n m f‖ = ‖f‖

name: sumEquiv_C
statement:
theorem sumEquiv_C (f : TateAlgebra K n) :
    sumEquiv K n m (C (1 : Fin m → ℝ) f) =
      eval₂ (Cφ := 1) (1 : Fin n → ℝ) (C (1 : Fin (m + n) → ℝ))
        (fun i ↦ X K (1 : Fin (m + n) → ℝ) (Fin.natAdd m i))
        (fun r ↦ by simp [norm_C])
        (norm_prod_pow_le_of_norm_le _ _ fun i ↦ by simp [norm_X]) f

name: sumEquiv_X
statement:
theorem sumEquiv_X (i : Fin m) :
    sumEquiv K n m (X (TateAlgebra K n) (1 : Fin m → ℝ) i) =
      X K (1 : Fin (m + n) → ℝ) (Fin.castAdd n i)

name: exists_norm_quotient_mk_eq
statement:
theorem exists_norm_quotient_mk_eq (f : TateAlgebra K n) :
    ∃ a₀ ∈ I, ‖Ideal.Quotient.mk I f‖ = ‖f - a₀‖
doc:
/-- The residue norm is attained: `‖f̄‖ = ‖f - a₀‖` for a nearest point `a₀ ∈ I` (strict
closedness of ideals, Layer 0). Source: BGR 6.1.1/2 ("The assertion follows directly from
Corollary 5.2.7/8"). -/

name: isClosed_ideal_quotient
statement:
theorem isClosed_ideal_quotient (J : Ideal (TateAlgebra K n ⧸ I)) :
    IsClosed (J : Set (TateAlgebra K n ⧸ I))
doc:
/-- Every ideal of a quotient of the Tate algebra is closed for the residue norm: its preimage in
`Tₙ` is an ideal, hence closed, and the residue map is a quotient map. Source: BGR 6.1.1/3 ("The
closedness of any ideal `𝔞 ⊂ A` follows … simply from the closedness of ideals in `Tₙ`"). -/

name: norm_quotient_mem_range_norm
statement:
theorem norm_quotient_mem_range_norm (x : TateAlgebra K n ⧸ I) :
    ‖x‖ ∈ Set.range (norm : K → ℝ)
doc: /-- The residue norm of `Tₙ ⧸ I` takes its values in `‖K‖`. Source: BGR 6.1.1/2. -/

name: exists_norm_smul_quotient_eq_one
statement:
theorem exists_norm_smul_quotient_eq_one {x : TateAlgebra K n ⧸ I} (hx : x ≠ 0) :
    ∃ a : K, ‖a • x‖ = 1
doc:
/-- Every nonzero element of `Tₙ ⧸ I` can be normed to length one by a scalar.
Source: BGR 6.1.1/2 ("each vector `≠ 0` in `A` can be normed to length 1 by multiplication with a
scalar"). -/

name: of_surjective
statement:
theorem of_surjective (hA : IsAffinoidAlgebra K A) (φ : A →ₐ[K] B) (hφ : Function.Surjective φ) :
    IsAffinoidAlgebra K B
doc:
/-- A surjective image of an affinoid algebra is affinoid. Source: BGR 6.1.1/3 ("`A/𝔞` is
`k`-affinoid, since `Tₙ → A → A/𝔞` is a continuous epimorphism"). -/

name: exists_algEquiv_quotient
statement:
theorem exists_algEquiv_quotient (hA : IsAffinoidAlgebra K A) :
    ∃ (n : ℕ) (I : Ideal (TateAlgebra K n)), Nonempty ((TateAlgebra K n ⧸ I) ≃ₐ[K] A)
doc:
/-- Every affinoid algebra is isomorphic to a quotient `Tₙ ⧸ I` of a Tate algebra; the ideal is
the kernel of the presentation. Source: BGR 6.1.1 ("`A` is isomorphic … to the residue algebra
`Tₙ/ker α`"). -/

name: isNoetherianRing
statement: theorem isNoetherianRing (hA : IsAffinoidAlgebra K A) : IsNoetherianRing A
doc:
/-- **Affinoid algebras are noetherian.** Source: BGR 6.1.1/3 ("`A ≅ Tₙ/ker α` is a Noetherian
Jacobson ring since `Tₙ` is such a ring"); Bosch 1.4, Prop. 2. -/

name: isJacobsonRing
statement: theorem isJacobsonRing (hA : IsAffinoidAlgebra K A) : IsJacobsonRing A
doc: /-- **Affinoid algebras are Jacobson rings.** Source: BGR 6.1.1/3; Bosch 1.4, Prop. 2. -/

name: norm_smul_le_of_normedAlgebra
statement: theorem norm_smul_le_of_normedAlgebra (k : K) (f : Restricted A c) : ‖k • f‖ ≤ ‖k‖ * ‖f‖
doc: /-- Scalars of `K` scale the Gauss norm of `Restricted A c` by at most their norm. -/

name: isPowerBounded_X
statement: theorem isPowerBounded_X (i : σ) : IsPowerBounded (X A (1 : σ → ℝ) i)
doc: /-- The variables of `A⟨X⟩` are power-bounded: `‖X i ^ k‖ = ‖1‖` for every `k ≥ 1`. -/

name: exists_forall_norm_prod_pow_le_of_isPowerBounded
doc:
/-- The monomials in finitely many power-bounded elements are uniformly bounded.
Source: BGR 6.1.1/4 ("Since `fᵢ ∈ Å` and `lim a_ν = 0`, the series … represents a well-defined
element of `A`"). -/

name: extendAlgHom
statement: noncomputable def extendAlgHom : Restricted A (1 : σ → ℝ) →ₐ[K] B

name: extendAlgHom_C
statement: theorem extendAlgHom_C (a : A) : extendAlgHom φ hφ b hb (C (1 : σ → ℝ) a) = φ a
doc: /-- The extension restricts to `φ` on the constants: `Φ | B = φ`. Source: BGR 6.1.1/4. -/

name: extendAlgHom_X
statement: theorem extendAlgHom_X (i : σ) : extendAlgHom φ hφ b hb (X A (1 : σ → ℝ) i) = b i
doc:
/-- The extension sends the variables to the given elements: `Φ(Xᵢ) = fᵢ`.
Source: BGR 6.1.1/4. -/

name: extendAlgHom_comp_toAlgHom
statement:
theorem extendAlgHom_comp_toAlgHom :
    (extendAlgHom φ hφ b hb).comp (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom K A (Restricted A (1 : σ → ℝ))) = φ
doc: /-- The extension restricts to `φ` on the constants, as `K`-algebra homomorphisms. -/

name: continuous_extendAlgHom
statement: theorem continuous_extendAlgHom : Continuous (extendAlgHom φ hφ b hb)
doc: /-- The extension is continuous. Source: BGR 6.1.1/4. -/

name: exists_forall_norm_extendAlgHom_le
statement:
theorem exists_forall_norm_extendAlgHom_le :
    ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ f, ‖extendAlgHom φ hφ b hb f‖ ≤ C * ‖f‖
doc: /-- The extension is bounded by the bounds of `φ` and of the monomials in `b`. -/

name: extendAlgHom_unique
statement:
theorem extendAlgHom_unique (ψ : Restricted A (1 : σ → ℝ) →ₐ[K] B) (hψ : Continuous ψ)
    (hC : ∀ a, ψ (C (1 : σ → ℝ) a) = φ a) (hX : ∀ i, ψ (X A (1 : σ → ℝ) i) = b i) :
    ψ = extendAlgHom φ hφ b hb
doc:
/-- **Uniqueness** in BGR 6.1.1/4: a continuous `K`-algebra homomorphism `A⟨X⟩ → B` that restricts
to `φ` on the constants and sends `X i` to `b i` is the extension. Source: BGR 6.1.1/4 ("`Φ` is the
unique continuous extension of `φ`"), via `algHom_ext_of_continuous`. -/

name: existsUnique_extend
statement:
theorem existsUnique_extend :
    ∃! ψ : Restricted A (1 : σ → ℝ) →ₐ[K] B,
      Continuous ψ ∧ (∀ a, ψ (C (1 : σ → ℝ) a) = φ a) ∧ ∀ i, ψ (X A (1 : σ → ℝ) i) = b i
doc: /-- BGR 6.1.1/4 as an existence-and-uniqueness statement. -/

name: extendAlgHom_ofId_eq_aeval
statement:
theorem extendAlgHom_ofId_eq_aeval [IsUltrametricDist K] (b : σ → B) (hb : ∀ i, ‖b i‖ ≤ 1)
    [NormOneClass B] :
    extendAlgHom (Algebra.ofId K B) (continuous_algebraMap K B) b
      (fun i ↦ isPowerBounded_of_norm_le_one (hb i)) =
      aeval (1 : σ → ℝ) b (fun i ↦ by simpa using hb i)
doc: /-- When `A = K` and `‖b i‖ ≤ 1`, the extension is the evaluation homomorphism of Layer 0. -/

name: isAffinoidGeneratingSystem_of_forall_exists_sum
statement:
theorem isAffinoidGeneratingSystem_of_forall_exists_sum [Fintype σ] (φ : A →ₐ[K] B)
    (hφ : Continuous φ) {b : σ → B} (hb : ∀ i, IsPowerBounded (b i))
    (hgen : ∀ y : B, ∃ q : σ → A, y = ∑ i, φ (q i) * b i) :
    IsAffinoidGeneratingSystem φ hφ b
doc:
/-- Elements `b` such that every element of `B` is `Σ φ(qᵢ) bᵢ` form an affinoid generating
system once they are power-bounded. Source: BGR 6.1.1/5 ("Then `Φ` is surjective"). -/

name: exists_forall_norm_smul_le_one
statement:
theorem exists_forall_norm_smul_le_one [Fintype σ] (a : σ → B) :
    ∃ c : K, c ≠ 0 ∧ ∀ i, ‖c • a i‖ ≤ 1
doc:
/-- In a normed algebra over a nontrivially normed field, finitely many elements can be rescaled
by one scalar into the unit ball. Source: BGR 6.1.1/5 ("We may assume `aᵢ ∈ Å`"). -/

name: exists_isAffinoidGeneratingSystem_of_finite
statement:
theorem exists_isAffinoidGeneratingSystem_of_finite (φ : A →ₐ[K] B) (hφ : Continuous φ)
    (hfin : φ.toRingHom.Finite) :
    ∃ (m : ℕ) (b : Fin m → B), IsAffinoidGeneratingSystem φ hφ b
doc:
/-- A continuous finite homomorphism `φ : A → B` admits an affinoid generating system over `A`:
rescale the module generators into the unit ball. Source: BGR 6.1.1/5. -/

name: continuous_algebraMap_restricted
statement:
theorem continuous_algebraMap_restricted (c : σ → ℝ) [Fact (∀ i, 0 < c i)] :
    Continuous (algebraMap A (Restricted A c))
doc: /-- The structure map `A → A⟨X⟩` is continuous (it is the constants). -/

name: mapAlgHom_C
statement: theorem mapAlgHom_C (a : A) : mapAlgHom α hα (C (1 : σ → ℝ) a) = C (1 : σ → ℝ) (α a)

name: mapAlgHom_X
statement: theorem mapAlgHom_X (i : σ) : mapAlgHom α hα (X A (1 : σ → ℝ) i) = X B (1 : σ → ℝ) i

name: coeff_mapAlgHom
statement:
theorem coeff_mapAlgHom (f : Restricted A (1 : σ → ℝ)) (t : σ →₀ ℕ) :
    coeff t (mapAlgHom α hα f).1 = α (coeff t f.1)
doc: /-- `mapAlgHom` acts on the coefficients. -/

name: surjective_mapAlgHom_of_surjective
statement:
theorem surjective_mapAlgHom_of_surjective [CompleteSpace A] (hsurj : Function.Surjective α) :
    Function.Surjective (mapAlgHom (σ := σ) α hα)
doc:
/-- A surjective continuous homomorphism of Banach algebras induces a surjection on strictly
convergent power series, by Banach's open mapping theorem: coefficients can be lifted with
controlled norms. Source: BGR 6.1.1/9 ("By BANACH's Theorem, `φ` is open and hence strict … we get
continuous epimorphisms `id_A ⊗̂ φ`"), through `ContinuousLinearMap.exists_preimage_norm_le`. -/

name: of_isAffinoidGeneratingSystem
doc:
/-- A Banach algebra with an affinoid generating system over `K` is affinoid.
Source: BGR 6.1.1, p. 223 ("If `Φ` is surjective, we call the elements `f₁, …, fₙ` a system of
affinoid generators of `A`. In particular, `A` is a `k`-affinoid algebra"). The converse for the
given norm on `B` needs the continuity theorem and is `exists_isAffinoidGeneratingSystem` in
`Affinoid/Continuity.lean`. -/

name: of_isAffinoidGeneratingSystem_tateAlgebra
statement:
theorem of_isAffinoidGeneratingSystem_tateAlgebra {n m : ℕ} (φ : TateAlgebra K n →ₐ[K] B)
    (hφ : Continuous φ) {b : Fin m → B} (hb : IsAffinoidGeneratingSystem φ hφ b) :
    IsAffinoidAlgebra K B
doc:
/-- A Banach algebra with an affinoid generating system over a Tate algebra is affinoid: compose
the extension `Tₙ⟨Y⟩ → B` with `T_{m+n} ≅ Tₙ⟨Y⟩`. Source: BGR 6.1.1/5 ("`Φ` is surjective, and
hence `A ∈ 𝔄`"). -/

name: of_finite_tateAlgebra
statement:
theorem of_finite_tateAlgebra {n : ℕ} (φ : TateAlgebra K n →ₐ[K] B) (hφ : Continuous φ)
    (hfin : φ.toRingHom.Finite) : IsAffinoidAlgebra K B
doc:
/-- **BGR 6.1.1/5 for the source `Tₙ`**: the target of a continuous finite `K`-algebra
homomorphism out of a Tate algebra into a Banach algebra is affinoid. -/

name: Ideal.forall_mem_of_forall_exists_eq_add_sum_mul_of_norm_lt_one
statement:
theorem Ideal.forall_mem_of_forall_exists_eq_add_sum_mul_of_norm_lt_one (I : Ideal A) {n : ℕ}
    (x : Fin n → A)
    (h : ∀ i, ∃ y ∈ I, ∃ c : Fin n → A, (∀ μ, ‖c μ‖ < 1) ∧ x i = y + ∑ μ, c μ * x μ) :
    ∀ i, x i ∈ I
doc:
/-- **The nonarchimedean Nakayama lemma** (BGR 1.2.4/6): if generators `x₁, …, xₙ` satisfy
`xᵢ ∈ I + Σ_μ 𝔫 x_μ` with `𝔫 = {‖c‖ < 1}`, then every `xᵢ` lies in `I`. Source: BGR 1.2.4/6
("Let `N` be a submodule of `M` such that there are elements `x₁, …, xₙ` in `M` with the property
`M ⊂ N + Σ Ǎ x_μ`. Then `N = M`"), proved through Mathlib's Nakayama lemma
`Submodule.le_of_le_smul_of_le_jacobson_bot` over `A°` with
`NormedRing.openUnitBallIdeal_le_jacobson_bot`. -/

name: Ideal.exists_forall_exists_eq_sum_mul_norm_le
statement:
theorem Ideal.exists_forall_exists_eq_sum_mul_norm_le {n : ℕ} (x : Fin n → A) (J : Ideal A)
    (hJ : IsClosed (J : Set A)) (hx : Ideal.span (Set.range x) = J) :
    ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∀ y ∈ J, ∃ a : Fin n → A, y = ∑ i, a i * x i ∧ ∀ i, ‖a i‖ ≤ C * ‖y‖
doc:
/-- A closed ideal `J` of a Banach algebra generated by `x₁, …, xₙ` admits bounded coefficients:
there is `C > 0` with every `y ∈ J` equal to `Σ aᵢ xᵢ` for some `aᵢ` with `‖aᵢ‖ ≤ C ‖y‖`, because
the continuous surjection `π : Aⁿ → J`, `(aᵢ) ↦ Σ aᵢ xᵢ`, of Banach spaces is open.
Source: BGR 3.7.2/1 ("By BANACH's Theorem, `π` is open"), through
`ContinuousLinearMap.exists_preimage_norm_le`. -/

name: Ideal.isClosed_coe_closure_restrictScalars
statement:
theorem Ideal.isClosed_coe_closure_restrictScalars (I : Ideal A) :
    IsClosed ((I.closure.restrictScalars K : Submodule K A) : Set A)
doc:
/-- The closure of an ideal in a normed `K`-algebra is a `K`-submodule: `Ideal.closure` restricted
to `K`-scalars. -/

name: Ideal.isClosed_of_fg_closure
statement:
theorem Ideal.isClosed_of_fg_closure (I : Ideal A) (hfg : I.closure.FG) :
    IsClosed (I : Set A)
doc:
/-- **BGR 3.7.2/1** in the form used for ideals: if the closure of an ideal `I` is finitely
generated, then `I` is closed. Source: BGR 3.7.2/1 ("Let `M` be a normed `A`-module such that the
completion `M̂` of `M` is a finite `A`-module. Then `M` is complete"). -/

name: LinearMap.continuous_of_isClosed_ker_of_finiteDimensional
statement:
theorem LinearMap.continuous_of_isClosed_ker_of_finiteDimensional [FiniteDimensional K F]
    (f : E →ₗ[K] F) (hf : IsClosed (LinearMap.ker f : Set E)) : Continuous f
doc:
/-- A linear map into a finite-dimensional normed space whose kernel is closed is continuous: it
factors through the quotient by its kernel, a finite-dimensional normed space, on which every
linear map is continuous. Source: BGR 3.7.5/1 ("the residue spaces `A/ker ψ` and `B/𝔟` provided
with the residue norms are finite-dimensional … Therefore `ψ̄` and hence `ψ` are continuous"),
via `LinearMap.quotKerEquivRange` and `LinearMap.continuous_of_finiteDimensional`. -/

name: AlgHom.continuous_quotient_mk_comp_of_isClosed
statement:
theorem AlgHom.continuous_quotient_mk_comp_of_isClosed (Φ : A →ₐ[K] B) (𝔟 : Ideal B)
    [IsClosed (𝔟 : Set B)] [FiniteDimensional K (B ⧸ 𝔟)]
    (hA : IsClosed ((𝔟.comap Φ : Ideal A) : Set A)) :
    Continuous ((Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ K 𝔟).comp Φ)
doc:
/-- The residue map `A → B ⧸ 𝔟` of `Φ` is continuous when `𝔟` is closed with finite-dimensional
quotient and `Φ⁻¹ 𝔟` is closed. Source: BGR 3.7.5/1 (the map `ψ := β ∘ Φ`). -/

name: AlgHom.continuous_of_forall_isClosed_of_finiteDimensional
statement:
theorem AlgHom.continuous_of_forall_isClosed_of_finiteDimensional (Φ : A →ₐ[K] B)
    (𝔅 : Set (Ideal B)) (hB : ∀ 𝔟 ∈ 𝔅, IsClosed (𝔟 : Set B))
    (hA : ∀ 𝔟 ∈ 𝔅, IsClosed ((𝔟.comap Φ : Ideal A) : Set A))
    (hfin : ∀ 𝔟 ∈ 𝔅, FiniteDimensional K (B ⧸ 𝔟)) (hinf : sInf 𝔅 = ⊥) : Continuous Φ
doc:
/-- **BGR 3.7.5/1**: a `K`-algebra homomorphism `Φ : A → B` of `K`-Banach algebras is continuous
if `B` has a family `𝔅` of ideals with (i) each `𝔟 ∈ 𝔅` and each `Φ⁻¹ 𝔟` closed, (ii) each
`B ⧸ 𝔟` finite-dimensional over `K`, (iii) `⋂ 𝔅 = 0`. Source: BGR 3.7.5/1, by the closed graph
theorem `LinearMap.continuous_of_seq_closed_graph`. -/

name: AlgHom.continuous_of_isNoetherianRing
statement:
theorem AlgHom.continuous_of_isNoetherianRing [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsNoetherianRing B]
    (𝔅 : Set (Ideal B)) (hfin : ∀ 𝔟 ∈ 𝔅, FiniteDimensional K (B ⧸ 𝔟)) (hinf : sInf 𝔅 = ⊥)
    (Φ : A →ₐ[K] B) : Continuous Φ
doc:
/-- **BGR 3.7.5/2**: every `K`-algebra homomorphism of a noetherian `K`-Banach algebra `A` into a
noetherian `K`-Banach algebra `B` having a family `𝔅` of ideals with finite-dimensional quotients
and zero intersection is continuous. Source: BGR 3.7.5/2 ("From Propositions 1 and 3.7.2/2, we
easily derive"). -/

name: AlgEquiv.continuous_symm_of_isNoetherianRing
statement:
theorem AlgEquiv.continuous_symm_of_isNoetherianRing [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsNoetherianRing B]
    (𝔅 : Set (Ideal B)) (hfin : ∀ 𝔟 ∈ 𝔅, FiniteDimensional K (B ⧸ 𝔟)) (hinf : sInf 𝔅 = ⊥)
    (e : A ≃ₐ[K] B) : Continuous e.symm
doc:
/-- **BGR 3.7.5/3**, second half: the inverse of such an isomorphism is continuous too, by the
open mapping theorem (`LinearEquiv.continuous_symm`). Hence "all Banach algebra structures on `B`
have the same underlying topological space". -/

name: AlgEquiv.exists_forall_norm_le_mul_of_isNoetherianRing
statement:
theorem AlgEquiv.exists_forall_norm_le_mul_of_isNoetherianRing [IsNoetherianRing A]
    [IsNoetherianRing B] (𝔅 : Set (Ideal B)) (hfin : ∀ 𝔟 ∈ 𝔅, FiniteDimensional K (B ⧸ 𝔟))
    (hinf : sInf 𝔅 = ⊥) (e : A ≃ₐ[K] B) :
    ∃ C C' : ℝ, (∀ a, ‖e a‖ ≤ C * ‖a‖) ∧ ∀ b, ‖e.symm b‖ ≤ C' * ‖b‖
doc: /-- **BGR 3.7.5/3** in terms of norms: the two complete algebra norms are equivalent. -/

name: finite_comp_ofTail_of_isMulDistinguishedX0
statement:
theorem finite_comp_ofTail_of_isMulDistinguishedX0 (φ : TateAlgebra K (n + 1) →+* A)
    (hφ : φ.Finite) {g : TateAlgebra K (n + 1)} {s : ℕ} (hg : IsMulDistinguishedX0 g s)
    (h0 : φ g = 0) : (φ.comp (ofTail K n)).Finite
doc:
/-- The Weierstrass finiteness theorem for a distinguished element of the kernel: a finite ring
homomorphism out of `T_{n+1}` killing an `X 0`-distinguished series restricts to a finite
homomorphism on `Tₙ`. Source: BGR 6.1.2/1 ("`α` induces a finite homomorphism `ᾱ : Tₙ/ωTₙ → A`.
By the Weierstrass Finiteness Theorem 5.2.3/4, the natural injection `T_{n−1} → Tₙ` induces a
finite monomorphism `β : T_{n−1} → Tₙ/ωTₙ`. Obviously, `ᾱ ∘ β` is finite"). -/

name: injective_mk_comp_ofTail_of_isMulDistinguishedX0
doc:
/-- The map `Tₙ → T_{n+1} ⧸ (g)` is injective for an `X 0`-distinguished `g`: a series without
`X 0` that is a multiple of `g` has two Weierstrass divisions by `g`, with remainders itself and `0`.
Source: BGR 6.1.2/1 ("the natural injection `T_{n−1} → Tₙ` induces a finite monomorphism
`β : T_{n−1} → Tₙ/ωTₙ`"), via `weierstrassDivision_r_unique`. -/

name: exists_finite_comp_shear_symm_comp_ofTail
statement:
theorem exists_finite_comp_shear_symm_comp_ofTail (β : TateAlgebra K (n + 1) →ₐ[K] A)
    (hβ : β.toRingHom.Finite) {f : TateAlgebra K (n + 1)} (hf : f ≠ 0) (h0 : β f = 0) :
    ∃ e : Fin n → ℕ,
      ((β.comp (shear K n e).symm.toAlgHom).comp (ofTailAlgHom K n)).toRingHom.Finite
doc:
/-- The induction step of BGR 6.1.2/1: a finite `β : T_{n+1} → A` with a nonzero element in its
kernel becomes, after a shear, finite on `Tₙ`. Source: BGR 6.1.2/1 ("Otherwise we can find a chart
`{X₁, …, Xₙ}` of `Tₙ` and a Weierstrass polynomial `ω ∈ T_{n−1}[Xₙ]` such that `ω ∈ ker α`"). -/

name: injective_of_nontrivial
statement:
theorem injective_of_nontrivial [Nontrivial A] (β : TateAlgebra K 0 →ₐ[K] A) :
    Function.Injective β
doc:
/-- A `K`-algebra homomorphism out of `T₀ = K` into a nonzero algebra is injective.
Source: BGR 6.1.2/1 ("The case `n = 0` is trivial"). -/

name: exists_finite_injective_comp
statement:
theorem exists_finite_injective_comp [Nontrivial A] (n : ℕ) (β : TateAlgebra K n →ₐ[K] A)
    (hβ : β.toRingHom.Finite) :
    ∃ d ≤ n, ∃ ψ : TateAlgebra K d →ₐ[K] TateAlgebra K n,
      (β.comp ψ).toRingHom.Finite ∧ Function.Injective (β.comp ψ)
doc:
/-- **BGR 6.1.2/1 (i)**: for a finite `K`-algebra homomorphism `β : Tₙ → A` into a nonzero
algebra there are `d ≤ n` and a `K`-algebra homomorphism `ψ : T_d → Tₙ` (a chart followed by the
inclusion of the last `d` variables) such that `β ∘ ψ` is finite and injective. Source: BGR 6.1.2/1
("there exist a chart `{X₁, …, Xₙ}` of `Tₙ` and an integer `d ≥ 0` such that `α | k⟨X₁, …, X_d⟩`
is finite and injective"), by induction on `n`. -/

name: exists_finite_injective_comp
statement:
theorem exists_finite_injective_comp (hB : IsAffinoidAlgebra K B) [Nontrivial A]
    (φ : B →ₐ[K] A) (hφ : φ.toRingHom.Finite) :
    ∃ (d : ℕ) (ψ : TateAlgebra K d →ₐ[K] B),
      (φ.comp ψ).toRingHom.Finite ∧ Function.Injective (φ.comp ψ)
doc:
/-- **BGR 6.1.2/1 (ii)**: a finite homomorphism `φ : B → A` of affinoid algebras with `A ≠ 0`
admits `ψ : T_d → B` with `φ ∘ ψ` finite and injective. Source: BGR 6.1.2/1 ("By choosing an
epimorphism `α : Tₙ → B` and applying the first statement to the map `φ ∘ α : Tₙ → A`"). -/

name: exists_finite_injective
statement:
theorem exists_finite_injective (hA : IsAffinoidAlgebra K A) [Nontrivial A] :
    ∃ (d : ℕ) (φ : TateAlgebra K d →ₐ[K] A), φ.toRingHom.Finite ∧ Function.Injective φ
doc:
/-- **Noether normalisation** (BGR 6.1.2/2; Bosch 1.2/10, 1.4/2): every nonzero affinoid algebra
is a finite extension of some Tate algebra `T_d`. -/

name: ringKrullDim_le_of_isIntegral_of_injective
statement:
theorem ringKrullDim_le_of_isIntegral_of_injective {R S : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing S]
    (f : R →+* S) (hf : f.IsIntegral) (hinj : Function.Injective f) :
    ringKrullDim R ≤ ringKrullDim S
doc:
/-- Going up: an injective integral ring homomorphism does not lower the Krull dimension, since
every chain of primes lifts (`Ideal.exists_ltSeries_of_hasGoingUp`). Source: BGR 6.1.2 (Remark),
citing Nagata, Corollary 10.10, for `dim A = dim T_d`. -/

name: ringKrullDim_eq_of_finite_injective
statement:
theorem ringKrullDim_eq_of_finite_injective {d : ℕ} (φ : TateAlgebra K d →ₐ[K] A)
    (hφ : φ.toRingHom.Finite) (hinj : Function.Injective φ) : ringKrullDim A = d
doc:
/-- The integer `d` of a Noether normalisation is the Krull dimension: `dim A = dim T_d = d`.
Source: BGR 6.1.2 (Remark). -/

name: exists_ringKrullDim_eq
statement:
theorem exists_ringKrullDim_eq (hA : IsAffinoidAlgebra K A) [Nontrivial A] :
    ∃ d : ℕ, ringKrullDim A = d
doc:
/-- The Krull dimension of a nonzero affinoid algebra is a natural number, the `d` of any Noether
normalisation. Source: BGR 6.1.2 (Remark) ("the integer `d` above is uniquely determined by the
algebra `A`"). -/

name: finiteDimensional_of_finite_zero
statement:
theorem finiteDimensional_of_finite_zero (φ : TateAlgebra K 0 →ₐ[K] A) (hφ : φ.toRingHom.Finite) :
    FiniteDimensional K A
doc: /-- Finite over `T₀` means finite-dimensional over `K`. -/

name: injective_factor_comp_of_injective
statement:
theorem injective_factor_comp_of_injective {R : Type*} [CommRing R] [IsReduced R]
    (𝔮 : Ideal A) (φ : R →+* A ⧸ 𝔮) (hφ : Function.Injective φ) :
    Function.Injective ((Ideal.Quotient.factor 𝔮.le_radical).comp φ)
doc:
/-- An injective homomorphism out of a reduced ring stays injective after passing to the quotient
by the radical of an ideal containing nothing of the image. Source: BGR 6.1.2/3 ("The composition
of `φ` with the canonical epimorphism `ϱ : A/𝔮 → A/rad 𝔮` is finite and injective (because `T_d`
is reduced)"). -/

name: _root_.Affinoid.TateAlgebra.eq_zero_of_isField
statement:
theorem _root_.Affinoid.TateAlgebra.eq_zero_of_isField {d : ℕ} (h : IsField (TateAlgebra K d)) :
    d = 0
doc:
/-- A Tate algebra that is a field has no variables: `d = 0`. Source: BGR 6.1.2/3 ("But then
`T_d` must itself be a field so that `d = 0`"), via `ringKrullDim_eq` and
`ringKrullDim_eq_zero_of_isField`. -/

name: finiteDimensional_quotient_of_radical_isMaximal
statement:
theorem finiteDimensional_quotient_of_radical_isMaximal (hA : IsAffinoidAlgebra K A)
    (𝔮 : Ideal A) (h : 𝔮.radical.IsMaximal) : FiniteDimensional K (A ⧸ 𝔮)
doc:
/-- **BGR 6.1.2/3**: if the radical of an ideal `𝔮` of an affinoid algebra `A` is maximal, then
`A ⧸ 𝔮` is a finite-dimensional `K`-vector space. Source: BGR 6.1.2/3; Bosch 1.4/3. -/

name: _root_.Ideal.isMaximal_comap_of_isAffinoidAlgebra
statement:
theorem _root_.Ideal.isMaximal_comap_of_isAffinoidAlgebra (hB : IsAffinoidAlgebra K B)
    (φ : A →ₐ[K] B) (𝔪 : Ideal B) [𝔪.IsMaximal] : (𝔪.comap φ).IsMaximal
doc:
/-- The preimage of a maximal ideal of an affinoid algebra under a `K`-algebra homomorphism is
maximal: `A ⧸ φ⁻¹ 𝔪` is a domain finite-dimensional over `K`, hence a field.
Source: roadmap §1.2.4 ("the preimage of a maximal ideal under a `K`-algebra map of affinoid
algebras is maximal"); BGR 6.1.2/3. -/

name: _root_.IsFractionRing.isLocalization_algebraMapSubmonoid_of_isIntegral
statement:
theorem _root_.IsFractionRing.isLocalization_algebraMapSubmonoid_of_isIntegral (R S : Type*)
    [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [IsDomain S] [Algebra R S] [Algebra.IsIntegral R S]
    (hinj : Function.Injective (algebraMap R S)) :
    IsLocalization (Algebra.algebraMapSubmonoid S (nonZeroDivisors R)) (FractionRing S)
doc:
/-- For an injective integral extension `R → S` of domains, the fraction field of `S` is the
localisation of `S` at the nonzero elements of `R`: every nonzero `s ∈ S` divides a nonzero element
of `R` (the constant term of a minimal integral equation). Source: BGR 6.1.2/4 ("`Q(A′)` is finite
over `Q(T_d)`"), the identification needed to apply `Module.Finite.of_isLocalization`. -/

name: _root_.FractionRing.finiteDimensional_of_finite
statement:
theorem _root_.FractionRing.finiteDimensional_of_finite (R S : Type*) [CommRing R] [IsDomain R]
    [CommRing S] [IsDomain S] [Algebra R S] [Module.Finite R S]
    (hinj : Function.Injective (algebraMap R S)) [Algebra (FractionRing R) (FractionRing S)]
    [IsScalarTower R (FractionRing R) (FractionRing S)] :
    FiniteDimensional (FractionRing R) (FractionRing S)
doc:
/-- The fraction field of a domain finite over a domain `R` is finite over the fraction field of
`R`. Source: BGR 6.1.2/4 ("`Q(A′)` is finite over `Q(T_d)`"). -/

name: isJapaneseRing
statement:
theorem isJapaneseRing {K : Type u} [NormedField K] [IsUltrametricDist K] [CompleteSpace K]
    [CharZero K] {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra K A] [IsDomain A]
    (hA : IsAffinoidAlgebra K A) : IsJapaneseRing A
doc:
/-- **BGR 6.1.2/4**: an affinoid integral domain is Japanese, in characteristic zero (where
`T_d` is Japanese by Layer 0). Source: BGR 6.1.2/4 ("there is a normalization map `φ : T_d → A` …
Since `T_d` is Japanese by Theorem 5.3.1/3, we see that `A'` is a finite `T_d`-module and a
fortiori a finite `A`-module"). -/

name: Ideal.sInf_maximalPowers_eq_bot
statement:
theorem Ideal.sInf_maximalPowers_eq_bot (A : Type*) [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A] :
    sInf (Ideal.maximalPowers A) = ⊥
doc:
/-- In a noetherian ring the powers of the maximal ideals intersect in zero: by Krull's
intersection theorem an element `f` of the intersection satisfies `(1 - m) f = 0` for some
`m ∈ 𝔪`, for every maximal `𝔪`, so its annihilator lies in no maximal ideal. Source: BGR 6.1.3
("KRULL's Intersection Theorem implies that for each `𝔪` there is an element `m ∈ 𝔪` such that
`(1 − m) f = 0`. Hence the annihilator of `f` is contained in no maximal ideal in `B`. Therefore,
`f = 0`"), via `Ideal.mem_iInf_smul_pow_eq_bot_iff`. -/

name: finiteDimensional_of_mem_maximalPowers
statement:
theorem finiteDimensional_of_mem_maximalPowers (hA : IsAffinoidAlgebra K A) {I : Ideal A}
    (hI : I ∈ Ideal.maximalPowers A) : FiniteDimensional K (A ⧸ I)
doc:
/-- Condition (i) of BGR 3.7.5/2 for an affinoid algebra: `dim_K A ⧸ 𝔪^ν < ∞`.
Source: BGR 6.1.3 ("We have `dim_k B/𝔟 < ∞` for all `𝔟 ∈ 𝔅` by Corollary 6.1.2/3"). -/

name: AlgHom.continuous_of_isAffinoidAlgebra
statement:
theorem AlgHom.continuous_of_isAffinoidAlgebra [IsNoetherianRing A] (hB : IsAffinoidAlgebra K B)
    (Φ : A →ₐ[K] B) : Continuous Φ
doc:
/-- **BGR 6.1.3/1**: every `K`-algebra homomorphism of a noetherian `K`-Banach algebra into an
affinoid algebra is continuous, for any complete algebra norms. Source: BGR 6.1.3/1 ("Since each
`B ∈ 𝔄` is Noetherian, we derive from Proposition 3.7.5/2"). -/

name: AlgEquiv.exists_forall_norm_le_mul_of_isAffinoidAlgebra
statement:
theorem AlgEquiv.exists_forall_norm_le_mul_of_isAffinoidAlgebra (hA : IsAffinoidAlgebra K A)
    (hB : IsAffinoidAlgebra K B) (e : A ≃ₐ[K] B) :
    ∃ C C' : ℝ, (∀ a, ‖e a‖ ≤ C * ‖a‖) ∧ ∀ b, ‖e.symm b‖ ≤ C' * ‖b‖
doc:
/-- **BGR 6.1.3/2** in terms of norms: any two complete algebra norms on an affinoid algebra are
equivalent. Source: roadmap §1.3.3 ("any two complete `K`-algebra norms on `A` are equivalent"). -/

name: AlgEquiv.isPowerBounded_map_iff_of_isAffinoidAlgebra
statement:
theorem AlgEquiv.isPowerBounded_map_iff_of_isAffinoidAlgebra (hA : IsAffinoidAlgebra K A)
    (hB : IsAffinoidAlgebra K B) (e : A ≃ₐ[K] B) (a : A) :
    IsPowerBounded (e a) ↔ IsPowerBounded a
doc:
/-- Power-boundedness is the same for all Banach norms on an affinoid algebra.
Source: roadmap §1.3.3. -/

name: AlgEquiv.isTopologicallyNilpotent_map_iff_of_isAffinoidAlgebra
statement:
theorem AlgEquiv.isTopologicallyNilpotent_map_iff_of_isAffinoidAlgebra
    (hA : IsAffinoidAlgebra K A) (hB : IsAffinoidAlgebra K B) (e : A ≃ₐ[K] B) (a : A) :
    IsTopologicallyNilpotent (e a) ↔ IsTopologicallyNilpotent a
doc:
/-- Topological nilpotence is the same for all Banach norms on an affinoid algebra.
Source: roadmap §1.3.3. -/

name: AlgHom.ext_of_isAffinoidGeneratingSystem
statement:
theorem AlgHom.ext_of_isAffinoidGeneratingSystem {σ : Type*} [_root_.Finite σ] (hA : IsAffinoidAlgebra K A)
    (hB : IsAffinoidAlgebra K B) {a : σ → A}
    (ha : IsAffinoidGeneratingSystem (Algebra.ofId K A) (continuous_algebraMap K A) a)
    {ψ₁ ψ₂ : A →ₐ[K] B} (h : ∀ i, ψ₁ (a i) = ψ₂ (a i)) : ψ₁ = ψ₂
doc:
/-- A homomorphism of affinoid algebras is determined by its values on an affinoid generating
system. Source: BGR 6.1.1/4 and 6.1.3/1; roadmap §1.1.4. -/

name: IsAffinoidAlgebra.exists_isAffinoidGeneratingSystem
statement:
theorem IsAffinoidAlgebra.exists_isAffinoidGeneratingSystem (hA : IsAffinoidAlgebra K A) :
    ∃ (n : ℕ) (a : Fin n → A),
      IsAffinoidGeneratingSystem (Algebra.ofId K A) (continuous_algebraMap K A) a
doc:
/-- An affinoid Banach algebra has an affinoid generating system over `K`: the images of the
variables under a presentation, which is continuous. Source: BGR 6.1.1, p. 223 (affinoid
generators); the converse of `IsAffinoidAlgebra.of_isAffinoidGeneratingSystem`. -/

name: IsAffinoidAlgebra.of_finite_of_continuous
statement:
theorem IsAffinoidAlgebra.of_finite_of_continuous (hA : IsAffinoidAlgebra K A) (φ : A →ₐ[K] B)
    (hφ : Continuous φ) (hfin : φ.toRingHom.Finite) : IsAffinoidAlgebra K B
doc:
/-- **BGR 6.1.1/5**: the target of a continuous finite `K`-algebra homomorphism out of an affinoid
algebra into a Banach algebra is affinoid. Source: BGR 6.1.1/5 ("We may assume `B = Tₙ` for some
`n`"), using the continuity of presentations. -/

name: IsAffinoidAlgebra.restricted
statement:
theorem IsAffinoidAlgebra.restricted (hA : IsAffinoidAlgebra K A) {σ : Type*} [_root_.Finite σ] :
    IsAffinoidAlgebra K (Restricted A (1 : σ → ℝ))
doc:
/-- `A⟨X₁, …, Xₘ⟩` is affinoid for an affinoid Banach algebra `A`: a presentation `Tₙ → A` lifts
to a surjection `Tₙ⟨X⟩ → A⟨X⟩` and `Tₙ⟨X⟩ ≅ T_{m+n}`. Source: BGR 6.1.4 ("If `A` is a
`k`-affinoid algebra … then the ring `A⟨X⟩` of strictly convergent power series over `A` is
`k`-affinoid"); BGR 6.1.1/9. -/

name: IsAffinoidAlgebra.exists_algEquiv_quotient_norm_comp_le
statement:
theorem IsAffinoidAlgebra.exists_algEquiv_quotient_norm_comp_le (hA : IsAffinoidAlgebra K A)
    (hB : IsAffinoidAlgebra K B) (φ : B →ₐ[K] A) :
    ∃ (n : ℕ) (I : Ideal (Restricted B (1 : Fin n → ℝ)))
      (e : (Restricted B (1 : Fin n → ℝ) ⧸ I) ≃ₐ[K] A),
      Continuous e ∧ Continuous e.symm ∧ ∀ b, ‖e.symm (φ b)‖ ≤ ‖b‖
doc:
/-- **BGR 6.1.3/3** (contractive renorming): for a homomorphism `φ : B → A` of affinoid algebras
there is a presentation `B⟨X⟩ ⧸ I ≅ A` of `A` over `B` whose residue norm is equivalent to the
given norm on `A` and for which `φ` is contractive. Source: BGR 6.1.3/3 ("the algebra norm on `A`
can be replaced by an equivalent one such that `φ` becomes contractive"). -/

name: inlAlgHom_C
statement: theorem inlAlgHom_C (a : A) : inlAlgHom K A σ τ (C (1 : σ → ℝ) a) = C (1 : σ ⊕ τ → ℝ) a

name: inrAlgHom_C
statement: theorem inrAlgHom_C (a : A) : inrAlgHom K A σ τ (C (1 : τ → ℝ) a) = C (1 : σ ⊕ τ → ℝ) a

name: inlAlgHom_comp_toAlgHom
statement:
theorem inlAlgHom_comp_toAlgHom :
    (inlAlgHom K A σ τ).comp (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom K A _) = IsScalarTower.toAlgHom K A _
doc: /-- The inclusions are `A`-algebra homomorphisms. -/

name: inrAlgHom_comp_toAlgHom
statement:
theorem inrAlgHom_comp_toAlgHom :
    (inrAlgHom K A σ τ).comp (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom K A _) = IsScalarTower.toAlgHom K A _

name: IsAffinoidTensorProduct.exists_algEquiv
statement:
theorem IsAffinoidTensorProduct.exists_algEquiv {T T' : Type v} [NormedCommRing T]
    [NormedAlgebra K T] [IsUltrametricDist T] [CompleteSpace T] [NormedCommRing T']
    [NormedAlgebra K T'] [IsUltrametricDist T'] [CompleteSpace T'] {ι₁ : B₁ →ₐ[K] T}
    {ι₂ : B₂ →ₐ[K] T} {ι₁' : B₁ →ₐ[K] T'} {ι₂' : B₂ →ₐ[K] T'}
    (h : IsAffinoidTensorProduct.{v} α₁ α₂ ι₁ ι₂) (h' : IsAffinoidTensorProduct.{v} α₁ α₂ ι₁' ι₂') :
    ∃ e : T ≃ₐ[K] T', Continuous e ∧ Continuous e.symm ∧
      e.toAlgHom.comp ι₁ = ι₁' ∧ e.toAlgHom.comp ι₂ = ι₂'
doc:
/-- **Uniqueness** of the affinoid tensor product: two pushouts are related by a unique continuous
isomorphism compatible with the structure maps. Source: BGR 3.1.1/2 ("characterizes the complete
tensor product"); roadmap §1.1.5 ("independent of the presentations up to canonical
isomorphism"). -/

name: IsAffinoidTensorProduct.of_algEquiv_left
statement:
theorem IsAffinoidTensorProduct.of_algEquiv_left {B₁' : Type*} [NormedCommRing B₁']
    [NormedAlgebra K B₁'] [IsUltrametricDist B₁'] [CompleteSpace B₁']
    (h : IsAffinoidTensorProduct.{v} α₁ α₂ ι₁ ι₂) (e : B₁' ≃ₐ[K] B₁) (he : Continuous e)
    (he' : Continuous e.symm) :
    IsAffinoidTensorProduct.{v} (e.symm.toAlgHom.comp α₁) α₂ (ι₁.comp e.toAlgHom) ι₂
doc: /-- The tensor-product property transports along a continuous isomorphism of the first factor. -/

name: isAffinoidTensorProduct_quotient_map
statement:
theorem isAffinoidTensorProduct_quotient_map [IsUltrametricDist K] [CompleteSpace K]
    [NormOneClass B₂] (hB₂ : IsAffinoidAlgebra K B₂) (α₂ : A →ₐ[K] B₂) (hα₂ : Continuous α₂)
    (𝔞 : Ideal A) [IsClosed (𝔞 : Set A)] :
    haveI : IsClosed ((𝔞.map α₂ : Ideal B₂) : Set B₂) := hB₂.isClosed_ideal _
    IsAffinoidTensorProduct.{v} (Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ K 𝔞) α₂
      (Ideal.quotientMapₐ (𝔞.map α₂) α₂ Ideal.le_comap_map) (Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ K (𝔞.map α₂))
doc:
/-- The quotient `B₂ ⧸ 𝔞 B₂` is an affinoid tensor product of `A ⧸ 𝔞` and `B₂` over `A`, for a
closed ideal `𝔞` with `B₂` affinoid. Source: BGR 6.1.1/11 (the case `B₁ = A`, `𝔟₁ = 𝔞`,
`𝔟₂ = 0`: `A/𝔞 ⊗̂_A B₂ = B₂/𝔞B₂`). -/

name: IsAffinoidTensorProduct.surjective_ι₂_of_surjective
statement:
theorem IsAffinoidTensorProduct.surjective_ι₂_of_surjective [IsUltrametricDist K]
    [CompleteSpace K] {B₂ T : Type v} [NormedCommRing B₂] [NormedAlgebra K B₂]
    [IsUltrametricDist B₂] [CompleteSpace B₂] [NormOneClass B₂] [NormedCommRing T]
    [NormedAlgebra K T] [IsUltrametricDist T] [CompleteSpace T] {α₂ : A →ₐ[K] B₂}
    {ι₁ : B₁ →ₐ[K] T} {ι₂ : B₂ →ₐ[K] T} (hB₂ : IsAffinoidAlgebra K B₂)
    (h : IsAffinoidTensorProduct.{v} α₁ α₂ ι₁ ι₂) (hα₁ : Continuous α₁)
    (hα₁' : Function.Surjective α₁) (hα₂ : Continuous α₂) : Function.Surjective ι₂
doc:
/-- **BGR 6.1.1/11**: if `α₁ : A → B₁` is surjective then so is `ι₂ : B₂ → B₁ ⊗̂_A B₂`, for `B₂`
affinoid: the tensor product is `B₂ ⧸ (ker α₁) B₂`. Source: BGR 6.1.1/11 ("the canonical map
`π : B₁ ⊗̂_A B₂ → B₁/𝔟₁ ⊗̂_A B₂/𝔟₂` is surjective"); roadmap §1.1.5. -/

statement:

doc:
/-- **The universal property**: for continuous `f₁ : B₁ → C`, `f₂ : B₂ → C` into a Banach algebra
agreeing on `A` there is a unique continuous `F : B₁ ⊗̂_A B₂ → C` with `F ∘ ι₁ = f₁` and
`F ∘ ι₂ = f₂`, namely the extension of BGR 6.1.1/4 with `X i ↦ f₁ (X̄ i)`, `Y j ↦ f₂ (Ȳ j)`.
Source: BGR 6.1.1/10–11 ("it is not hard to see that these induced maps satisfy the universal
property characterizing the complete tensor product"). -/

residue classes of all polynomials in `X ⊕ Y`. Source: roadmap §1.1.5 ("`B₁ ⊗̂_A B₂` receives the
algebraic tensor product `B₁ ⊗_A B₂` with dense image"). -/

name: IsGeneralisedFractions.exists_algEquiv
statement:
theorem IsGeneralisedFractions.exists_algEquiv {A' A'' : Type v} [NormedCommRing A']
    [NormedAlgebra K A'] [IsUltrametricDist A'] [CompleteSpace A'] [NormedCommRing A'']
    [NormedAlgebra K A''] [IsUltrametricDist A''] [CompleteSpace A''] {φ₀ : A →ₐ[K] A'}
    {φ₀' : A →ₐ[K] A''} (h : IsGeneralisedFractions.{v} φ₀ f g)
    (h' : IsGeneralisedFractions.{v} φ₀' f g) :
    ∃ e : A' ≃ₐ[K] A'', Continuous e ∧ Continuous e.symm ∧ e.toAlgHom.comp φ₀ = φ₀'
doc:
/-- **Uniqueness** of generalised rings of fractions: two of them are related by a unique continuous
isomorphism over `A`. Source: BGR 6.1.4 ("both algebras satisfy the same universal property"). -/

name: IsGeneralisedFractions.trans
statement:
theorem IsGeneralisedFractions.trans {A'' : Type*} [NormedCommRing A''] [NormedAlgebra K A'']
    [IsUltrametricDist A''] [CompleteSpace A''] {φ₁ : A' →ₐ[K] A''} {m' n' : ℕ} {f' : Fin m' → A}
    {g' : Fin n' → A} (h : IsGeneralisedFractions.{v} φ₀ f g)
    (h' : IsGeneralisedFractions.{v} φ₁ (φ₀ ∘ f') (φ₀ ∘ g')) :
    IsGeneralisedFractions.{v} (φ₁.comp φ₀) (Fin.append f f') (Fin.append g g')
doc:
/-- **Associativity** (BGR 6.1.4/2): `A⟨f, g⁻¹⟩⟨f', g'⁻¹⟩ = A⟨f, f', g⁻¹, g'⁻¹⟩`, at the level of
universal properties. Source: BGR 6.1.4 ("it follows from Proposition 2 that we have associativity
in the following sense: `A⟨f₁, …, f_{m−1}, g₁⁻¹, …, g_{n−1}⁻¹⟩⟨f_m, gₙ⁻¹⟩ = A⟨f₁, …, f_m, g₁⁻¹, …,
gₙ⁻¹⟩`"). -/

name: IsGeneralisedFractions.of_isUnit
statement:
theorem IsGeneralisedFractions.of_isUnit (hg : ∀ j, IsUnit (g j)) (hf : ∀ i, IsPowerBounded (f i))
    (hg' : ∀ j, IsPowerBounded (↑(hg j).unit⁻¹ : A)) :
    IsGeneralisedFractions.{v} (AlgHom.id K A) f g
doc:
/-- When the `g j` are already units of `A` with power-bounded inverses and the `f i` are
power-bounded, `A` itself is `A⟨f, g⁻¹⟩`. Source: BGR 6.1.4 ("`A⟨h⁻¹⟩` is defined in two ways when
`h ∈ A` is a unit. However … both definitions coincide in this special case"). -/

name: IsRationalFractions.isGeneralisedFractions_of_one
statement:
theorem IsRationalFractions.isGeneralisedFractions_of_one (h : IsRationalFractions.{v} φ₀ f 1) :
    IsGeneralisedFractions.{v} φ₀ f (Fin.elim0 : Fin 0 → A)
doc:
/-- A rational ring of fractions with denominator `1` is the generalised ring of fractions with no
denominators. Source: BGR 6.1.4 ("our definition of `A⟨f/g⟩` is compatible with the one given
before, if the `fᵢ` or `g` are units"). -/

statement: theorem continuous_toFractions : Continuous (toFractions K A f g)

theorem toFractions_mul_mk_X_inr (j : Fin n) :

doc: /-- The residue classes of the `Yⱼ` invert the `gⱼ`. -/

statement:
theorem toFractions_f (i : Fin m) :
    toFractions K A f g (f i) = Ideal.Quotient.mk _ (X A (1 : Fin m ⊕ Fin n → ℝ) (Sum.inl i))
doc: /-- The `fᵢ` are the residue classes of the `Xᵢ`, hence power-bounded. -/

name: isGeneralisedFractions_toFractions
statement:
theorem isGeneralisedFractions_toFractions [IsUltrametricDist K] [CompleteSpace K] [NormOneClass A]
    (hA : IsAffinoidAlgebra K A) :
    haveI : IsClosed ((fractionIdeal A f g : Ideal _) : Set (Restricted A (1 : Fin m ⊕ Fin n → ℝ)))
doc:
/-- **BGR 6.1.4/1–2**: `A⟨X, Y⟩ ⧸ (X − f, gY − 1)` has the universal property of `A⟨f, g⁻¹⟩`.
Source: BGR 6.1.4 ("the canonical map `A → A⟨X, Y⟩/(X − f, gY − 1)` also satisfies the universal
property stated in Proposition 1. Namely, let `φ : A → B` be a continuous homomorphism as in
Proposition 1. Then `φ` extends to a continuous homomorphism `φ″ : A⟨X, Y⟩ → B`, `X ↦ φ(f)`,
`Y ↦ φ(g)⁻¹`, with `(X − f, gY − 1) ⊂ ker φ″`"), for `A` affinoid (so that the ideal is closed and
the quotient is a Banach algebra). -/

name: continuous_toRational

name: isUnit_toRational
statement:
theorem isUnit_toRational (hgen : ∃ (a : A) (a' : Fin m → A), a * g + ∑ i, a' i * f i = 1) :
    IsUnit (toRational K A f g g)
doc:
/-- `g` becomes a unit in `A⟨f/g⟩` when `f₁, …, fₘ, g` generate the unit ideal:
`(a + Σ aᵢ X̄ᵢ) g = a g + Σ aᵢ fᵢ = 1`. Source: BGR 6.1.4 ("which shows that `g` is a unit in
`A′`"). -/

name: toRational_mul_inv
statement:
theorem toRational_mul_inv (hgen : ∃ (a : A) (a' : Fin m → A), a * g + ∑ i, a' i * f i = 1)
    (i : Fin m) :
    toRational K A f g (f i) * (↑(isUnit_toRational K A f g hgen).unit⁻¹ : RationalFractions A f g) =
      Ideal.Quotient.mk _ (X A (1 : Fin m → ℝ) i)
doc: /-- `X̄ᵢ = fᵢ / g` in `A⟨f/g⟩`. Source: BGR 6.1.4 ("Moreover, `X̄ᵢ = fᵢ/g` in `A′`"). -/

name: isPowerBounded_toRational_div
statement:
theorem isPowerBounded_toRational_div
    (hgen : ∃ (a : A) (a' : Fin m → A), a * g + ∑ i, a' i * f i = 1) (i : Fin m) :
    IsPowerBounded (toRational K A f g (f i) *
      (↑(isUnit_toRational K A f g hgen).unit⁻¹ : RationalFractions A f g))

name: isRationalFractions_toRational
statement:
theorem isRationalFractions_toRational [IsUltrametricDist K] [CompleteSpace K] [NormOneClass A]
    (hA : IsAffinoidAlgebra K A)
    (hgen : ∃ (a : A) (a' : Fin m → A), a * g + ∑ i, a' i * f i = 1) :
    haveI : IsClosed ((rationalIdeal A f g : Ideal _) : Set (Restricted A (1 : Fin m → ℝ)))
doc:
/-- **BGR 6.1.4/3–4**: `A⟨X⟩ ⧸ (gX − f)` has the universal property of `A⟨f/g⟩`. Source: BGR 6.1.4
("It is now a straightforward verification to see that also `A′ = A⟨X⟩/(gX − f)` satisfies the
universal property stated in Proposition 3"). -/

name: denseRange_awayLift
statement:
theorem denseRange_awayLift (hgen : ∃ (a : A) (a' : Fin m → A), a * g + ∑ i, a' i * f i = 1) :
    DenseRange (awayLift K A f g hgen)
doc:
/-- **`A[g⁻¹]` is dense in `A⟨f/g⟩`**: the residue classes of the polynomials in `X` are the images
of the `Σ b_ν (f/g)^ν`. Source: BGR 6.1.4 ("The completion of `A[g⁻¹]` is denoted by `A⟨f/g⟩`"),
the density half; roadmap §1.4.2. -/

statement:
theorem baseChangeAlgHom_tmul (c : K') (f : TateAlgebra K n) :

name: exists_sum_smul_mapBase
statement:
theorem exists_sum_smul_mapBase [CompleteSpace K] {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] (b : Module.Basis ι K K')
    (g : TateAlgebra K' n) : ∃ h : ι → TateAlgebra K n, g = ∑ k, b k • mapBase K K' n (h k)
doc:
/-- Every series over `K'` is a finite sum `Σ eₖ • gₖ` with `gₖ ∈ Tₙ(K)`, for a `K`-basis `e` of
`K'`: the coordinate functionals of a finite-dimensional normed space are continuous, so the
coordinates of the coefficients tend to zero. Source: BGR 6.1.1/8, with BGR 3.7.1 ("these
extensions carry always the product topology"). -/

theorem norm_smul_X_pow (hc : ∀ i, ρ i ^ s i * ‖c i‖ = 1) (i : Fin n) :
    ‖c i • X K ρ i ^ s i‖ = 1
doc: /-- `‖cᵢ Xᵢ^{sᵢ}‖_ρ = 1` when `ρᵢ^{sᵢ} ‖cᵢ‖ = 1`. Source: BGR 6.1.5/4 ("Then `|cᵢ Xᵢ^{sᵢ}|_ϱ = 1`"). -/

name: injective_rescaleAlgHom
statement:
theorem injective_rescaleAlgHom (hs : ∀ i, s i ≠ 0) :
    Function.Injective (rescaleAlgHom ρ s c hc)
doc:
/-- The rescaling acts on coefficients by `a_μ ↦ a_μ c^μ` placed at `μ s`; in particular it is
injective. Source: BGR 6.1.5/4 ("a monomorphism"). -/

name: isRestricted_shiftCoeff
statement:
theorem isRestricted_shiftCoeff (hs : ∀ i, s i ≠ 0) (hc0 : ∀ i, c i ≠ 0) (f : Restricted K ρ)
    (l : Fin n →₀ ℕ) :
    IsRestricted (1 : Fin n → ℝ) (fun μ : Fin n →₀ ℕ ↦
      coeff (Finsupp.ofSupportFinite (fun i ↦ μ i * s i) (Set.toFinite _) + l) f.1 *
        ∏ i, (c i)⁻¹ ^ μ i : MvPowerSeries (Fin n) K)
doc:
/-- The series `g_λ = Σ_μ a_{μs+λ} c^{−μ} X^μ` of BGR 6.1.5/4 lies in `Tₙ`, since
`|a_{μs+λ} c^{−μ}| = |a_{μs+λ}| ϱ^{μs+λ} ϱ^{−λ} → 0`. -/

name: finite_rescaleAlgHom
statement:
theorem finite_rescaleAlgHom (hs : ∀ i, s i ≠ 0) (hc0 : ∀ i, c i ≠ 0) :
    (rescaleAlgHom ρ s c hc).toRingHom.Finite
doc:
/-- **`T_{n,ρ}` is a finite `Tₙ`-module** via the rescaling, generated by the monomials `X^λ`,
`0 ≤ λᵢ < sᵢ`: `f = Σ_λ φ(g_λ) X^λ`. Source: BGR 6.1.5/4 ("We have `f = Σ_λ φ(g_λ) X^λ` so that
`T_{n,ϱ}` is a finite `Tₙ`-module via `φ`; the monomials `X^λ`, `0 ≤ λᵢ < sᵢ`, are generators"). -/

name: isAffinoidAlgebra_of_forall_exists_pow_eq_norm
statement:
theorem isAffinoidAlgebra_of_forall_exists_pow_eq_norm
    (h : ∀ i, ∃ (s : ℕ) (c : K), s ≠ 0 ∧ c ≠ 0 ∧ ρ i ^ s = ‖c‖) :
    IsAffinoidAlgebra K (Restricted K ρ)
doc:
/-- **BGR 6.1.5/4, the "if" half**: `T_{n,ρ}` is affinoid when every `ρᵢ` is a root of an element
of `|K^×|`. Source: BGR 6.1.5/4 ("Thus, `T_{n,ϱ}` is `k`-affinoid by Proposition 6.1.1/5, and half
of the theorem is proved"). -/

name: exists_summable_not_isRestricted
statement:
theorem exists_summable_not_isRestricted {ρ : ℝ} (hρ : 0 < ρ) :
    ∃ f : PowerSeries K, (∀ x : K, ‖x‖ < ρ → Summable fun ν ↦ coeff ν f * x ^ ν) ∧
      ¬ IsRestricted ρ f
doc:
/-- **The open-disc example** (BGR 6.1.5): for every `ρ > 0` there is a power series converging at
every `x` with `‖x‖ < ρ` which is not in `T_{1,ρ}`, namely `Σ aₙ Xⁿ` with `‖aₙ‖ ρⁿ ∈ [‖π‖⁻¹, 1]`.
Source: BGR 6.1.5 ("there are power series `f = Σ a_ν X^ν` converging on `B⁻(0, ϱ)`, which do not
satisfy the condition `lim |a_ν| ϱ^ν = 0`, so that `f ∉ T_{1,ϱ}` in this case"). -/

name: finrank_quotient_X_sq_sub
statement:
theorem finrank_quotient_X_sq_sub {a : K} (ha : ‖a‖ < 1) :
    Module.finrank K (TateAlgebra K 1 ⧸
      Ideal.span {X K (1 : Fin 1 → ℝ) 0 ^ 2 - C (1 : Fin 1 → ℝ) a}) = 2
doc:
/-- `K⟨X⟩ ⧸ (X² − a)` for `‖a‖ < 1` is a two-dimensional `K`-vector space with basis `1, X̄`: the
polynomial `X² − a` is a Weierstrass polynomial, so every series has a unique remainder of degree
less than two. Source: Layer 0, `IsWeierstrassPolynomial.existsUnique_remainder`. -/

name: ker_aeval_eq_span
doc:
/-- The kernel of evaluation at a point `a` of the closed unit disc is `(X − a)`: Weierstrass
division by the Weierstrass polynomial `X − a`. -/

statement:
